newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RALLYING-MAKINEN PULLS AWAY IN RALLY AUSTRALIA.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-MAKINEN PULLS AWAY IN RALLY AUSTRALIA.

text.p: Tommi Makinen of Finland mastered atrocious conditions to build a comfortable lead on the second day of the Rally of Australia, seventh round of the world championship.
Heavy rain caused havoc, forcing organisers to cancel two stages after four of the first six cars were stranded in a deep river crossing.
But Mitsubishi driver Makinen sailed through unscathed and will become world champion for the first time unless positions change during the third and final day on Monday.

"I don't understand why the others aren't faster. I was driving quite safely, smoothly and nicely, just one big slide round the corners. It is no problem," said Makinen who opened a lead of one minute 22 seconds.

Sweden's Kenneth Eriksson, one of only two drivers with a mathematical chance of depriving Makinen of the title, forced his Subaru into second place ahead of Carlos Sainz's Ford. That was despite stopping in the river on the 14th stage, then running into electrical trouble which filled his car with smoke because of the amount of water it had taken aboard.
In his determination to keep going Eriksson sucked muddy water from the engine's turbocharger through a plastic pipe before his mechanics made lasting repairs.
"I feel that Tommi is going a little too fast for all of us. But tomorrow is still a long day," he said.
Spaniard Sainz, the third title contender, also stopped in the river and slid off the road twice in some of the worst conditions ever seen on the rally.

World champion Colin McRae of Britain had another disappointing day. Choosing the hardest available tyres meant his Subaru had no grip at first and he skated off into the bushes on a fast, muddy right hand corner for a few seconds in the afternoon.
"It's difficult. I don't know how Tommi does these times. The car's really struggling as though it hasn't got any power," he said.
Fellow Britain Richard Burns holds fifth palce in his Mitsubishi but took no risks on some of the fastest and narrowest stages in the world championship.
